own_solution.law: Newton's second law in the plane of the turntable for a coin co-rotating: F = m r sqrt(omega^4 + alpha^2), omega = alpha t
assumptions: static friction supplies both centripetal and tangential acceleration

T0819.regime: maximum static friction at or above the required force (no slipping); 95 mN > 12.47 mN

T2F1F.regime: maximum static friction at or above the required force (no slipping); 95 mN > 12.47 mN

notes: omega = 0.9 x 4 = 3.6 rad/s; a_c = 12.96 x 0.08 = 1.0368 m/s^2; a_t = 0.9 x 0.08 = 0.072 m/s^2; |a| = sqrt(1.07495 + 0.00518) = 1.03930 m/s^2. F = 0.012 x 1.0393 = 12.47 mN. With a 5 g washer taped on (coin+washer 17 g, washer at the same radius, treated as one small body): F = 0.017 x 1.0393 = 17.67 mN (friction from the turntable on the coin-washer assembly). With either sentence, required force stays below 95 mN, so the friction limit sentences are K. Dish/washer-in-dish and earlier-trial sentences are D.
